title: Colombia Presidential Election First Round: Cepeda Wins, Runoff vs. De la Espriella June 21; ELN Ceasefire Holds; Petro Era Ends
detail: May 31, 2026 — Iván Cepeda won the first round of Colombia's presidential election, advancing to a June 21, 2026 runoff against conservative Abelardo De la Espriella. Cepeda — a senator from the Pacto Histórico coalition and veteran human rights lawyer known for his work exposing military 'false positives' (extrajudicial killings) and FARC accountability — emerged as the first-round leader with approximately 44-45% of the vote according to exit polls and initial counts, well ahead of De la Espriella's approximately 31%. No candidate secured the outright 50%+1 majority required to avoid a runoff; third-placed Paloma Valencia (Democratic Center) received approximately 14%. Outgoing President Gustavo Petro's 'Total Peace' initiative — which achieved neither ELN peace (talks collapsed January 2025 after the Catatumbo massacre) nor FARC-EMC demobilization (Mordisco broke off talks citing unfulfilled 2016 accord) — ends with Petro's term today. The ELN's 4-day election ceasefire held throughout voting day with no significant election-related violence reported by security forces or the CNE. The June 21 runoff is the defining moment for Colombia's peace architecture: Cepeda pledges to restart ELN negotiations, continue the JEP transitional justice system, and reopen FARC-EMC talks on the basis of 2016 accord implementation; De la Espriella has pledged to immediately terminate all negotiations with armed groups and pursue a military-first security approach. Crisis Group assessed in 'Colombia's Polls Mark a Forking Path' (May 2026) that consolidated right-wing voters from Valencia's ~14% and other conservative factions could shift the June 21 outcome decisively, potentially making De la Espriella the runoff favorite.

title: US-Iran Deal Remains Unsigned Day 3 Post-Tentative Agreement; Hormuz Blocked Week 14; Lebanon Political Track June 2–3 Approaches
detail: May 31, 2026 — Three days after CNN confirmed a 'tentative agreement' between the US and Iran (May 28), President Trump has not formally signed or announced a 'final determination' on the deal. CNBC reported on May 29 that Trump ended a White House meeting on Iran without issuing a final decision, despite VP Vance acknowledging just a day earlier that only 'a couple of language points' remained unresolved. IRGC General Rezaei escalated on May 30 with a warning that Iran would 'attack the blockade' if Trump betrays the tentative agreement. The Strait of Hormuz remains physically closed on May 31 — approximately 750 vessels trapped, approximately $6B/month in Iranian oil exports blocked, and US gasoline prices holding at approximately $4.48/gallon entering their 14th week of closure. The 60-day MOU framework (Phase 1: mines cleared, Hormuz reopens, US lifts blockade, Iran oil sales resume; Phase 2: nuclear talks on enrichment suspension and HEU removal) remains the baseline. Pakistan Army Chief Gen. Asim Munir continues as the principal back-channel intermediary. The congressional opposition bloc (52 senators, 177 House members) continues to constrain Trump's domestic room to formally announce a deal permitting enrichment. The Lebanon-Israel political track (Round 4) is scheduled for June 2–3 in Washington — the next critical milestone for the Lebanon ceasefire process, with the 45-day extension (in force since May 17) counting down toward its ~June 29 expiry. The Ukraine-Russia June 2 Istanbul Round 2 — proposed after the Rubio-Lavrov meeting on May 29 — is now tomorrow, with a 1,200-for-1,200 prisoner exchange reportedly in the works but ceasefire prospects assessed as low.
